text:
alex: hitting a reproducible goroutine leak when cancelling generator streams in the Go sampleapp. CPU and goroutines climb over repeated runs.
talia: which SDK version and sample?
alex: go-sdk v0.12.1, examples/generator/stream-example. command: `for i in {1..200}; do ./stream-example --timeout 1s; done` shows goroutines increasing.
alex: minimal pattern: start a stream, read first token, cancel ctx. sometimes iter.Close() is not called. code: `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), time.Second); iter, _ := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req); if iter.Next() { _ = iter.Token() }; cancel()`
ron: does iter.Err() report context.Canceled?
alex: yes, Err() often == context.Canceled, but stack traces show auth refresher retry loops and net/http persistConn stacks.
talia: sounds like the auth refresher spawns retry workers that don't observe the request ctx and keep retrying after cancel.
ron: can you paste the trimmed goroutine dump?
alex: (trimmed) `goroutine 10234 [semacquire]: internal/poll.runtime_pollWait ... net/http.(*persistConn).roundTrip ... github.com/redwood/sdk/auth.(*Refresher).retryWorker ... created by github.com/redwood/sdk/auth.(*Refresher).Start`
talia: I can repro with a tight timeout. filing internal ticket DEVEX-8421. fix ideas: have refresher select on reqCtx.Done(), ensure iter.Close() cancels per-request auth ctx, or drop work for canceled request ids.
ron: interim workaround: wrap HTTP transport to check ctx.Done() and abort requests; not ideal but reduces leak.
talia: I'll open a draft PR to pass per-request ctx into auth refresh calls and add a stress test that asserts goroutine count stabilizes.
ciara-bot: Draft PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/912 (ci queued).
alex: also suggest updating the gen quickstart to show `defer iter.Close()` and mention auth/retry caveats in the streaming section.
talia: good call. I'll add a short note in devex quickstart and the example README. thanks for the report. :thumbsup:
